first_setup.title: Set Up BRUH Claude
first_setup.description:
This creates:
- A **conversation agent** that appears in Settings > Voice Assistants
- **Usage limit sensors** that track your Anthropic account usage

You can add more agents with different personalities later using the **Add Service** button.

data_description.name: This name appears in Voice Assistants and on the Devices page.

add_agent.title: Add Another Agent
add_agent.description:
Create a new conversation agent with its own personality. Each agent gets its own model, system prompt, and timeout.

**Usage sensors are shared** — they're account-wide and already set up.

data_description.name: A unique name for this agent (e.g. 'Sarcastic Claude', 'Kitchen Assistant').
data_description.model: Which Claude model this agent uses. Sonnet is fast and balanced, Opus is the most capable, Haiku is the fastest and cheapest.
data_description.system_prompt: Defines who this agent is: identity, tone, and verbosity. It takes precedence over the built-in style — device control, tools, and the area map are appended automatically and stay out of its way. Include a length rule (e.g. keep spoken replies short) if your persona tends to ramble.
data_description.timeout: Maximum time in seconds to wait for Claude to respond.
data_description.denied_services: Services this agent may NOT call, even by voice — enforced in the MCP server, so it covers every device tool. Pick common risky ones or type your own: exact like lock.unlock, or a whole domain like lock.* . Leave empty to allow everything.

hassio_confirm.title: BRUH Claude Discovered
hassio_confirm.description:
The BRUH Terminal add-on has been detected. Click Submit to create a conversation agent and usage limit sensors.

You can add more agents with different personalities later from the integration page.

add_insight.title: Add Insight Job
add_insight.description:
Claude runs this job on a schedule and writes a markdown report to a sensor.

Getting started: pick a template and a schedule — that's enough. After creating it, the job runs once within ~2 minutes; you'll get a notification with a dashboard card ready to paste (also available any time as the sensor's card_yaml attribute). Run it any time with the job's Run now button.

To read or customize the template's full prompt, open Configure on the created entry — it shows the exact text that runs.

data_description.insight_prompt: Leave empty to use the template. Anything here overrides it. Supports Home Assistant templating — states(...), state_attr(...) — rendered before each run.
data_description.interval_minutes: 0 disables interval runs (daily time or Run now button only).
data_description.daily_at: 24-hour HH:MM, e.g. 07:30. Works alone or together with the interval.
data_description.model: Haiku is fastest, Opus is most thorough. Default uses the terminal's model.
data_description.notify_service: Push every successful report to this notify service, e.g. mobile_app_bens_iphone. Empty disables.

error.addon_not_running: The BRUH Terminal add-on does not appear to be running. Start the add-on and try again.
error.no_features: Please enable at least one feature.
error.invalid_daily_at: Daily time must be HH:MM (24-hour), e.g. 07:30.

add_memory.name: Add memory fact
add_memory.description: Queue a durable fact about your home for Claude's long-term memory.

fact.name: Fact
fact.description: The fact to remember, e.g. We call the office lamp 'the beacon'.

source.name: Source
source.description: Where this fact came from (defaults to service).

confidence.name: Confidence
confidence.description: How certain the fact is (defaults to medium).

answer_question.name: Answer memory question
answer_question.description: Answer an open question from Claude's memory system. The answer is recorded and also queued as a memory fact.

source.name: Source
source.description: Where this answer came from (defaults to service).

aliases.name: Aliases

floor_id.name: Floor

delete_area.name: Delete area

set_area_aliases.name: Set area aliases

aliases.name: Aliases
aliases.description: The full new list of aliases.

add_device_to_area.name: Add device to area
add_device_to_area.description: Assign one or more devices to an area.

remove_device_from_area.name: Remove device from area

add_entity_to_area.name: Add entity to area
add_entity_to_area.description: Assign one or more entities to an area (overrides the device's area).

remove_entity_from_area.name: Remove entity from area
remove_entity_from_area.description: Remove one or more entities from whatever area they are in.

create_floor.name: Create floor
create_floor.description: Create a new floor. Returns the new floor_id as response data.

aliases.name: Aliases
aliases.description: Alternative names, used by voice assistants.

delete_floor.name: Delete floor
delete_floor.description: Delete a floor. Areas on it are left without a floor. Set dry_run to preview the areas that would lose the floor.

dry_run.name: Dry run
dry_run.description: When on, only report what would change — nothing is modified.

add_area_to_floor.name: Add area to floor
add_area_to_floor.description: Place one or more areas on a floor.

area_id.name: Areas
area_id.description: Areas to place on the floor.

remove_area_from_floor.name: Remove area from floor
remove_area_from_floor.description: Remove one or more areas from whatever floor they are on.

area_id.name: Areas
area_id.description: Areas to remove from their floor.

create_label.name: Create label
create_label.description: Create a new label. Returns the new label_id as response data.

color.name: Color
color.description: Label color: a theme color name (e.g. red, blue, amber) or hex code.

delete_label.name: Delete label
delete_label.description: Delete a label. It is removed from everything it was applied to. Set dry_run to preview everything currently carrying the label.

dry_run.name: Dry run
dry_run.description: When on, only report what would change — nothing is modified.

add_label.name: Add label
add_label.description: Apply one or more labels to entities, devices, and/or areas. At least one target is required.

remove_label.name: Remove label
remove_label.description: Remove one or more labels from entities, devices, and/or areas. At least one target is required.

rename_entity.name: Rename entity
rename_entity.description: Set the friendly name override of one or more entities.

change_entity_id.name: Change entity ID
change_entity_id.description: Change an entity's ID (e.g. light.shelly_abc123 to light.kitchen_ceiling). Automations and dashboards referencing the old ID must be updated separately. The response lists automations/scripts/scenes that reference the old id; set dry_run to preview without renaming.

new_entity_id.name: New entity ID
new_entity_id.description: The new entity ID, same domain.

dry_run.name: Dry run
dry_run.description: When on, only report what would change — nothing is modified.

enable_entity.name: Enable entity
enable_entity.description: Enable one or more disabled entities. Takes effect after the owning integration reloads.

disable_entity.name: Disable entity
disable_entity.description: Disable one or more entities. They stop updating and are removed from the UI.

hide_entity.name: Hide entity
hide_entity.description: Hide one or more entities from auto-generated dashboards and voice assistants. They keep working.

unhide_entity.name: Unhide entity
unhide_entity.description: Unhide one or more hidden entities.

delete_orphaned_entities.name: Delete orphaned entities
delete_orphaned_entities.description: Remove registry entries for entities whose integration no longer provides them (state shows as 'restored'). Runs as a dry run by default and returns the list of affected entities as response data.

dry_run.name: Dry run
dry_run.description: When on (default), only report what would be removed.

entity_id.name: Entities
entity_id.description: Restrict the cleanup to these entities. Each one is re-verified as orphaned; anything still provided by an integration is skipped and reported, never deleted. Omit to target every orphaned entity.

rename_device.name: Rename device
rename_device.description: Set the user-facing name of a device.

enable_device.name: Enable device
enable_device.description: Enable one or more disabled devices (including their parent hub devices if those were disabled).

disable_device.name: Disable device
disable_device.description: Disable one or more devices and all their entities. A parent hub device is also disabled once none of its children remain enabled.

enable_integration.name: Enable integration
enable_integration.description: Enable one or more disabled integration config entries.

disable_integration.name: Disable integration
disable_integration.description: Disable one or more integration config entries and everything they provide. Set dry_run to preview the affected entries and entity counts.

dry_run.name: Dry run
dry_run.description: When on, only report what would change — nothing is modified.

reload_integration.name: Reload integration
reload_integration.description: Reload one or more integration config entries — like pressing Reload on the integration page.

create_zone.name: Create zone
create_zone.description: Create a new zone for location tracking.

radius.name: Radius
radius.description: Radius of the zone in meters (default 100).

passive.name: Passive
passive.description: Passive zones are only used for automations, not shown on the map.

delete_zone.name: Delete zone
delete_zone.description: Delete one or more UI-created zones. Set dry_run to preview the zones that would be deleted.

dry_run.name: Dry run
dry_run.description: When on, only report what would change — nothing is modified.

add_device_tracker_to_person.name: Add device tracker to person
add_device_tracker_to_person.description: Attach one or more device trackers to a person for presence detection.

remove_device_tracker_from_person.name: Remove device tracker from person
remove_device_tracker_from_person.description: Detach one or more device trackers from a person.

create_repair_issue.name: Create repair issue
create_repair_issue.description: Create a custom issue in Settings > System > Repairs — a persistent, dismissible way to surface something that needs the user's attention. Returns the issue_id as response data.

description.name: Description
description.description: Full description shown when the issue is opened.

severity.name: Severity
severity.description: How serious the issue is (default warning).

persistent.name: Persistent
persistent.description: Keep the issue across Home Assistant restarts.

issue_id.name: Issue ID
issue_id.description: Optional stable ID so the issue can be removed or replaced later. Auto-generated when omitted.

remove_repair_issue.name: Remove repair issue
remove_repair_issue.description: Remove a previously created repair issue by its issue ID.

issue_id.name: Issue ID
issue_id.description: The issue_id used (or returned) when the issue was created.

import_blueprint.name: Import blueprint
import_blueprint.description: Import an automation or script blueprint from a URL (Home Assistant community forum, GitHub, or GitHub Gist). Returns the blueprint domain, name, and file path as response data.

url.name: URL
url.description: The URL to import the blueprint from.

import_statistics.name: Import statistics
import_statistics.description: Import or backfill long-term statistics rows. Use an entity ID (sensor.gas_meter) for recorder statistics, or an external ID (bruh:solar_forecast) for external statistics; the source is derived automatically. Runs as a dry run by default: the response reports the affected time range and existing rows that would be overwritten. Pass dry_run: false to actually import — existing rows in the window are overwritten and cannot be restored without a recorder DB backup.

has_mean.name: Has mean
has_mean.description: Whether the rows carry mean/min/max values (measurements).

has_sum.name: Has sum
has_sum.description: Whether the rows carry sum values (metered totals like energy).

unit_of_measurement.name: Unit
unit_of_measurement.description: Unit of measurement of the values.

stats.name: Rows
stats.description: List of statistics rows. Each row needs a start timestamp (top of an hour) plus mean/min/max and/or state/sum values.

dry_run.name: Dry run
dry_run.description: When on (default), only report the affected window and existing rows — nothing is written.

enable_user.name: Enable user
enable_user.description: Re-enable one or more disabled Home Assistant user accounts.

user_id.name: User IDs
user_id.description: IDs of the users to enable.

disable_user.name: Disable user
disable_user.description: Disable one or more Home Assistant user accounts. Owner accounts and system-generated users are protected and cannot be disabled.

user_id.name: User IDs
user_id.description: IDs of the users to disable.

find_orphaned_references.name: Find orphaned references
find_orphaned_references.description: Scan every automation, script, and scene for references to entities Home Assistant doesn't know (renamed, deleted, or typo'd). Returns the findings as response data; optionally raises a repair issue listing them.

create_issue.name: Create repair issue
create_issue.description: Also surface the findings in Settings > System > Repairs.

update_dashboard.name: Update dashboard
update_dashboard.description: Replace a storage-mode dashboard's configuration. The previous configuration is automatically backed up first (last 20 kept per dashboard) and the backup name is returned as response data, so any edit can be undone with restore_dashboard. YAML-mode dashboards are refused. url_path is required — pass the literal "default" to target the default dashboard. Saving onto a never-saved (auto-generated) dashboard requires take_control: true. Set view_index to replace a single view instead of the whole config, and dry_run to preview the resolved target and change summary without writing.

config.name: Configuration
config.description: The full dashboard configuration object including the complete views list — or, when view_index is set, a single view object.

url_path.name: Dashboard
url_path.description: The dashboard's URL path (e.g. lovelace-lights), or the literal "default" for the default dashboard.

take_control.name: Take control
take_control.description: Confirm saving onto a never-saved (auto-generated) dashboard, taking permanent manual control of it.

view_index.name: View index
view_index.description: Replace only this view (0-based); config must then be a single view object.

dry_run.name: Dry run
dry_run.description: When on, only report what would change — nothing is modified.

restore_dashboard.name: Restore dashboard
restore_dashboard.description: Restore a storage-mode dashboard from a backup made by update_dashboard. Restores the most recent backup unless a specific backup name is given.

url_path.name: Dashboard
url_path.description: The dashboard's URL path. Omit for the default dashboard.

backup.name: Backup
backup.description: A specific backup file name from a previous update_dashboard response. Omit for the most recent.

reset_dashboard_config.name: Reset dashboard config
reset_dashboard_config.description: Delete a dashboard's STORED configuration (after backing it up), reverting it to auto-generated. The sanctioned way to clear a dashboard config — never use raw lovelace/config websocket commands. The dashboard itself stays registered; restore_dashboard brings the config back from the backup.

url_path.name: Dashboard
url_path.description: The dashboard's URL path, or the literal "default" for the default dashboard.

dry_run.name: Dry run
dry_run.description: When on, only report what would change — nothing is modified.

create_helper.name: Create helper
create_helper.description: Create a helper of any storage-backed type: input_boolean, input_number, input_select, input_text, input_datetime, counter, timer, or schedule. Type-specific options pass through and are validated by the helper's own schema. Returns the new helper's id and entity_id as response data.

helper_type.name: Type
helper_type.description: Which kind of helper to create.

options.name: Options
options.description: Type-specific options, e.g. min/max/step for input_number, options list for input_select, duration for timer, has_date/has_time for input_datetime.

delete_helper.name: Delete helper
delete_helper.description: Delete one or more UI-created helpers of any storage-backed type. Helpers defined in YAML are refused with a clear error. Set dry_run to preview the helpers that would be deleted.

dry_run.name: Dry run
dry_run.description: When on, only report what would change — nothing is modified.

update_zone.name: Update zone
update_zone.description: Move, resize, rename, or restyle an editable zone. Only the fields you pass are changed.

latitude.name: Latitude
latitude.description: New latitude of the zone center.

longitude.name: Longitude
longitude.description: New longitude of the zone center.

passive.name: Passive
passive.description: Passive zones are only used for automations.

set_entity_aliases.name: Set entity aliases
set_entity_aliases.description: Replace an entity's voice-assistant aliases — the alternative names Assist listens for.

aliases.name: Aliases
aliases.description: The full new list of aliases.

set_entity_icon.name: Set entity icon
set_entity_icon.description: Set an icon override on one or more entities. Omit the icon to clear the override and return to the default.

icon.name: Icon
icon.description: The icon to set. Omit to clear the override.

create_dashboard.name: Create dashboard
create_dashboard.description: Create a new storage-mode dashboard. The URL path must contain a hyphen (e.g. lovelace-lights). Returns the new dashboard's url_path and id as response data.

url_path.name: URL path
url_path.description: URL path for the dashboard; must contain a hyphen.

show_in_sidebar.name: Show in sidebar
show_in_sidebar.description: Show the dashboard in the sidebar (default on).

require_admin.name: Admin only
require_admin.description: Only admins can see this dashboard.

delete_dashboard.name: Delete dashboard
delete_dashboard.description: Delete a storage-mode dashboard. Its configuration is backed up first (same backup store as update_dashboard) and the backup name is returned as response data, so a deletion can be recovered by recreating the dashboard and restoring. Set dry_run to preview the dashboard and whether a backup would be created.

dry_run.name: Dry run
dry_run.description: When on, only report what would change — nothing is modified.

add_dashboard_resource.name: Add dashboard resource
add_dashboard_resource.description: Register a dashboard resource — the JavaScript module or stylesheet of a custom card (e.g. /hacsfiles/... or /local/...). Returns the resource id as response data. Duplicate URLs are refused.

remove_dashboard_resource.name: Remove dashboard resource
remove_dashboard_resource.description: Remove a registered dashboard resource by its URL.

url.name: URL
url.description: The URL of the resource to remove.

create_person.name: Create person
create_person.description: Create a person, optionally linked to a Home Assistant user and with initial device trackers. Returns the person's id as response data.

user_id.name: User
user_id.description: Home Assistant user to link (from get_registry users).

delete_person.name: Delete person
delete_person.description: Delete a UI-created person. YAML-defined persons are refused. Set dry_run to preview the person and their device trackers.

dry_run.name: Dry run
dry_run.description: When on, only report what would change — nothing is modified.

create_user.name: Create user
create_user.description: Create a Home Assistant user account, optionally with a local username/password login (they must be provided together; password minimum 8 characters). Returns the new user_id as response data.

name.name: Name
name.description: Display name of the new user.

admin.name: Administrator
admin.description: Give the user admin rights (default off).

delete_user.name: Delete user
delete_user.description: Delete one or more Home Assistant user accounts and their credentials. Owner accounts and system-generated users are protected and cannot be deleted. Set dry_run to preview the accounts that would be deleted.

user_id.name: User IDs
user_id.description: IDs of the users to delete.

dry_run.name: Dry run
dry_run.description: When on, only report what would change — nothing is modified.

confirm.title: Restart Home Assistant
confirm.description:
The BRUH Claude integration has been updated to version {version}. Home Assistant will restart to load the new version.

This will briefly interrupt all automations and connections.
